title: fix(driver-sqlite-wasm): handle a failing background flush instead of rejecting unhandled
body:
Fixes #23635
Clause-②: no

A flush that fails in the background in `driver-sqlite-wasm` is now handled at the producer: reported once, at `error`, with the database file named, and the file stays dirty so a later flush retries. It no longer reaches the process as an unhandled rejection. An awaited `flush()` / `close()` still throws to its caller.

## What changed

`packages/drivers/driver-sqlite-wasm/src/wasm-connection.ts`, one file:

- The three fire-and-forget flushes (`markDirty` under `on-write`, the `debounced:N` timer, and the flush deferred past a transaction's close in `noteTransactionControl`) now call one private helper, `flushInBackground()`, in place of three bare `void this.flush()`.
- On rejection the helper calls `reportBackgroundFlushFailure()`: one line at `error` (at `warn` for a logger that has no `error`) naming the file, the consequence (writes since the last good flush are not on disk while the database keeps answering from memory and looks healthy) and the fix. It reports once per failure episode: a latch is set by the first report and cleared when a flush actually writes, so `on-write` does not log once per write (AGENTS.md, "Degradation log levels": say it once, at the first degradation). The reporter never throws, because a throwing logger inside a rejection handler would recreate the unhandled rejection.
- `flush()` is unchanged except that it clears the latch after a landed write. It still re-marks `dirty` and rethrows, so the next flush retries and an awaited caller still gets the error. `close()` is untouched.
- The exported type surface is unchanged: `error` is read off the injected logger when it has one (`console` does). Declaring it on the exported `logger` option type would be a Clause-② widening and a `minor`; see Acceptance notes.

One patch changeset: `.changeset/23635-sqlite-wasm-background-flush-failure.md`.

## The pin, and how it asserts "no unhandled rejection"

`src/sqlite-wasm-background-flush-failure.test.ts`, 10 tests. The assertion is direct: every test attaches its own `process.on('unhandledRejection')` listener and requires that it saw nothing once the flush chain has settled. It awaits the chain tail and then 20 ms of event-loop turn, so no fixed sleep races the flush, and it does not lean on Vitest's run-level unhandled-error report.

- One test per call site (on-write, debounce timer, transaction close). Each makes the flush fail by removing the database's directory, as the dogfood teardown did, and asserts: no unhandled rejection, exactly one `error` line naming the file, `dirty` still set.
- Retry: once the directory is back, the next write's flush lands, and a second connection reads back every row written during the failure.
- Once per episode: three failed writes give one line; after a flush lands, a new failure reports again.
- Report robustness: a `warn`-only logger still hears it, at `warn`; a logger that throws produces no unhandled rejection.
- CONTROL: an awaited `flush()` rejects with `ENOENT` and does not also log, `dirty` stays set and a later `flush()` resolves; `close()` rejects with `ENOENT`.
- Through the driver: the dogfood race itself (a live `SqliteWasmDriver` on `on-write`, its directory removed, the next insert) is reported, and the public `driver.flush()` still rejects.

### Ablation

Each leg mutated `wasm-connection.ts` through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor hit once, blob changed on disk, restore proven: blob equal to HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty). The test imports `src` directly, so no `dist/` rebuild leg applies. The first attempt of the once-guard leg was refused by the tool as a no-op (its replacement was a substring of its anchor) and redone with a distinct replacement.

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| on-write site back to bare `void this.flush()` | the on-write test and the 5 tests that drive on-write fail (6 of 10); debounce and transaction tests stay green |
| debounce site back to bare | exactly the debounce test fails (1 of 10) |
| transaction-close site back to bare | exactly the transaction test fails (1 of 10) |
| helper body back to bare `void this.flush()` (all three sites) | 8 of 10 fail; the two CONTROL tests stay green |
| once-guard removed | the once-per-episode test fails (1 of 10) |
| latch reset after a landed write removed | the once-per-episode test fails (1 of 10) |
| logger try/catch removed | the throwing-logger test fails (1 of 10) |
| `warn` fallback removed | the `warn`-only test fails (1 of 10) |
| `this.dirty = true` on failure removed (existing line) | 8 of 10 fail, including the retry test |

On the unmutated tree the file passes 10 of 10.

## Verification

At `aa42889b36`. The patch round changed one thing: the private `logger` field's type is now one literal, with `warn` required and `error` optional. Every run below was repeated at this head.

- `pnpm check:optional-error-sink` (a wide-population family that `--commands` does not print) was red at `e3b5224c85`, on the old intersection type. It exits 0 at this head: 37 sinks declare an optional `error` beside a required `warn`, and 0 are `no-fallback`. Both blocks `dispatch-gates.mjs` prints on every run were also run, each with its own command: the artifact-roster block, 53 of 53 exit 0, and the wide-population block, 11 of 11 exit 0.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/driver-sqlite-wasm typecheck`: exit 0. Whole package suite: 37 files, 685 tests, all pass.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 62 commands from this tree; all 62 ran at this commit and exited 0, and `--ran` reconciles 62 derived, 62 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED. One of them, `check:logger-receiver-detach`, was red on my first spelling (a logger channel read off `this.logger` into a local) and is fixed in the last commit. `pnpm check:durability-log-level` is also green.
- eslint with `--no-inline-config` on the two changed source files, `--format json`: 2 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings. The repo config never enables type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`, no typed rules; see the note near line 328 of `eslint.config.mjs`), so this diff cannot move the verdict of an untouched file. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is left to CI.
- NOT MEASURED: the Dogfood Regression Gate (2/3). It is CI-owned and the race is intermittent, so a local run could not prove it; the pin reproduces the mechanism deterministically instead.

## Measured, out of scope and not fixed here: where the refused boot's driver is left open

The seat filed this as #23644.

A boot that fails after a plugin's `start()` connected a driver never tears that driver down.

- Connect: `ObjectQLPlugin.start` (`packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts`, `await this.ql?.init()`) reaches `driver.connect()` in `ObjectQLEngine.init` (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`, the `for (const [name, driver] of this.drivers)` loop).
- Failure: the ownership guard throws at `kernel:ready`, Phase 3 of `ObjectKernel.bootstrap()` (`packages/core/src/kernel.ts`, `await this.context.trigger('kernel:ready')`).
- Why nothing closes it: `rollbackStartedPlugins()` is called only inside the Phase 2 branch for a plugin whose `start()` failed. The outer `catch (error)` of `bootstrap()` sets the state to `stopped`, releases the signal listeners and rethrows; the comment there states that `shutdown()` on such a kernel is a no-op. So no plugin `destroy()` runs, including `DefaultDatasourcePlugin.destroy` (`packages/runtime/src/default-datasource-plugin.ts`), the path that disconnects the default datasource. The two in-process callers, `Runtime.start()` (`packages/runtime/src/runtime.ts`) and `bootStack` (`packages/verify/src/harness.ts`, `await kernel.bootstrap()`), add no teardown of their own.
- Probe (core `dist`, scratch script outside the repo): plugin A's `start()` records a connect and its `destroy()` records a disconnect; plugin B hooks `kernel:ready` and throws. Result: `["driver.connect()", "bootstrap rejected: refused at kernel:ready", "shutdown() returned"]`, with no disconnect. Positive control, same kernel but plugin B's `start()` throws (Phase 2 rollback): `["driver.connect()", "driver.disconnect() via destroy()", "bootstrap rejected: ..."]`, so the probe can see a destroy when one happens.

## Acceptance notes

- Typing `error` on the exported `WasmConnectionOptions['logger']` would let a typed caller pass a logger with `error` without a cast, and it is the declared home of this behaviour. It widens a published surface (Clause-② `yes (widening)`, `minor`), which the card's claim declared `no`, so it is not done here. The seat can take that as its own card.
- `SqliteWasmDriver.connect()` registers a `beforeExit` handler (`packages/drivers/driver-sqlite-wasm/src/sqlite-wasm-driver.ts`) that calls `void this.flush().catch(() => { /* ignore */ })`, so a flush that fails at process exit is swallowed with no log. Read from source, not run. It sits outside this card's file surface and is not filed.
